purpose: Stable, public architecture vocabulary for SAP ABAP OO, RAP, CAP, clean core and integration design reviews.
note: Patterns are independent explanations, not an SAP-certified reference implementation. Sources and applicability are in linked human pages.

patterns.name: Thin Entry Point
patterns.summary: A BAdI, user exit or IDoc hook should route work, not become the application.
patterns.review_phrase: Use a Thin Entry Point: the enhancement should translate the SAP contract and delegate to an application service.

patterns.name: Strategy / Policy Resolver
patterns.summary: Replace a forest of country, channel or organization CASE branches with named policies.
patterns.review_phrase: Use Strategy with a Policy Resolver; the organization rule is a replaceable decision, not a new IF in the transport layer.

patterns.name: Repository + Dependency Injection
patterns.summary: Hide database and SAP API calls behind a testable boundary.
patterns.review_phrase: Use Repository + DI. The business decision should not know whether its input came from SQL, EML or a released API.

patterns.name: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
patterns.summary: Translate legacy or external meanings once, before they reach core rules.
patterns.review_phrase: Put an Anti-Corruption Layer in front of the domain; source-system codes must not control downstream business rules.

patterns.name: Delta-Aware Merge / Patch Semantics
patterns.summary: A missing field, an explicitly cleared field and a deleted segment must not mean the same thing.
patterns.review_phrase: We need Delta-Aware Merge: resolve MSGFN and field presence before lookup or write, then protect fields explicitly.

patterns.name: Decision Table / Rules as Data
patterns.summary: When the business owns many combinations, stop encoding them as nested IF statements.
patterns.review_phrase: Make this a Decision Table. The rule combinations belong in governed data; the evaluator should stay boring.

patterns.name: Released API Boundary (Clean Core)
patterns.summary: Depend on an intentional SAP contract, not on a convenient internal table or implementation detail.
patterns.review_phrase: We need a Released API Boundary. Please show the API's release status and the extension ownership model.

patterns.name: Managed RAP Business Object
patterns.summary: Let the RAP runtime own ordinary persistence, locking and transactional plumbing for custom data.
patterns.review_phrase: This is custom owned persistence: start with Managed RAP rather than hand-written CRUD.

patterns.name: Unmanaged RAP Facade
patterns.summary: Modernize the service contract around proven transactional logic without rewriting the engine first.
patterns.review_phrase: Use an Unmanaged RAP Facade so the existing engine stays the single writer; prove the save-sequence contract first.

patterns.name: RAP Validation vs Determination vs Action
patterns.summary: Use the RAP behavior concept that matches the business meaning.
patterns.review_phrase: This needs a Determination, not an Action; the user did not request an explicit command. Keep the invariant in Validation.

patterns.name: RAP Draft Workflow
patterns.summary: Separate 'I am editing' from 'the active business state has changed'.
patterns.review_phrase: Use RAP Draft if the real requirement is safe multi-step editing; do not invent an extra 'temporary' active status.

patterns.name: CAP Service Facade
patterns.summary: Expose a purpose-built service contract instead of publishing the database model verbatim.
patterns.review_phrase: Use a CAP Service Facade. Let the consumer see a stable use-case contract, not the underlying storage or remote ERP schema.

patterns.name: CAP Event Handler / Lifecycle Hook
patterns.summary: Add custom logic around CAP's service events while keeping the service contract in charge.
patterns.review_phrase: Use a CAP Event Handler for the service lifecycle; do not create a second controller that bypasses CAP authorization and transaction rules.

patterns.name: Idempotent Consumer
patterns.summary: A retry must not create a second business effect.
patterns.review_phrase: Add an Idempotent Consumer. We must tolerate duplicate delivery, not hope the broker sends once.

patterns.name: Transactional Outbox / Commit-Then-Publish
patterns.summary: Never claim an event was delivered just because business code reached its last line.
patterns.review_phrase: Use a Transactional Outbox or platform-managed event queue, and make the consumer idempotent.

patterns.name: Retry + Dead Letter / Quarantine
patterns.summary: Retry a temporary outage; quarantine bad data; never run an infinite retry storm.
patterns.review_phrase: Add a Retry Budget and Dead Letter policy: operators must know what failed, why it stopped and how to replay safely.
